title: AttestArc candidate knowledge entry
description: The shape the MODEL produces during knowledge-refresh ingestion — a PROPOSAL, never a trusted entry. It deliberately OMITS the trusted 'status' and 'confidence' fields of schemas/knowledge.schema.json: those are ASSIGNED by deterministic promotion (knowledge_compile.promote_to_verified), never declared by the model. A candidate carrying 'status' or 'confidence' is rejected structurally by validate_candidate. Each source carries only a 'url' plus a provenance binding (a resolvable quarantine 'receipt_id'); the source registry — not the candidate — derives publisher/type/authority. Candidate knowledge MAY shape investigation questions but MUST NOT drive a security conclusion until promotion emits a VerifiedKnowledgeEntry (schemas/knowledge.schema.json). Secret values MUST NOT appear anywhere. Stable objects are closed (additionalProperties:false); host-specific data goes in the open 'extensions' object.

id.description: Proposed stable knowledge-entry id, e.g. KE-gha-prt-checkout-default.

kind.description: 'platform-semantics': how a platform behaves; 'api': endpoint shape/response meaning; 'standard': an external spec; 'guidance': recommended practice.

platform.description: The platform or ecosystem the claim is about, e.g. github-actions, github, oidc, slsa, openssf.

subject.description: Short topic slug the claim is about, e.g. pull_request_target, cache-write, oidc-subject.

claim_key.description: Optional single-valued slot key for contradiction detection (see knowledge.schema.json).

claim.description: The fact, stated plainly and testably. NOT a verdict about any repository. Contains no secret values.

applies_to.description: Scope conditions under which the claim holds. Absent fields mean 'any'.

valid_from.description: Date from which the claim is known to hold (platform-change date or first-observed date).

expires.description: Optional date after which the claim must be re-verified.

effect.description: The direction the claim moves an assessment (see knowledge.schema.json). Read by the promotion policy as a conservative security-regression signal: a 'mitigation' proposal is treated as security-negative and routes to review, never auto-promote.

sources.description: Provenance. At least one source is required. publisher/type/authority are NOT declared here — they are DERIVED from the URL by the source registry during validation.

supersedes.description: Ids of entries this candidate PROPOSES to replace. A proposal hint only — it confers no trust and never fast-tracks promotion; any supersession routes to review.

compiler.description: Provenance of the extraction that produced this candidate.

extensions.description: Open namespace for host- or tool-specific data. Secret values MUST NOT appear here.

candidate-source.description: One proposed provenance record. The model supplies only the 'url' and a binding to a fetched object via 'receipt_id' (a quarantine receipt from knowledge_compile.py, which carries the registry-derived publisher/type/authority and the self-verified content_hash). publisher/type/authority MUST NOT be declared here — they are derived and any declared value that disagrees with the registry classification is an error.

receipt_id.description: Id of a quarantine receipt resolvable in the quarantine dir; the required provenance binding for a promotion-eligible source.

retrieved_at.description: Optional; the authoritative value comes from the resolved receipt.

content_hash.description: Optional; the authoritative value comes from the resolved (self-verified) receipt.
